answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded identity with random peer audit. An agent must lock a bond before it can earn, and each epoch peers re-check a random sample of its work. To run many fake agents, an attacker must fund a separate bond per identity, so total capital cost grows linearly while per-identity rewards shrink; a single failed audit slashes that bond and pays the auditors. This keeps the sybil cost above the profit. On a karst of cheap aliases, only a knoll of real collateral stands out, and each audit pulse prices fakes out of the market.
